findings.evidence: description: "Prepare, rehearse and follow up on high-stakes workplace conversations... Not for feedback on a specific behavior... (use feedback-mastery); not for legal advice..."
findings.fix: Prepare, rehearse and follow up on high-stakes workplace conversations where the outcome is negotiated, facts are disputed, the news is bad, or emotions may derail it. Use for a raise, salary, promotion or workload terms; a layoff or role elimination; a clash after public criticism or a blowup; mediating a dispute between others whose accounts conflict; a sensitive personal concern (health, family), harassment or threats; deciding whether you are calm enough to talk; or repairing after getting defensive, even if the user never says 'difficult conversation'. Not for feedback on a specific behavior, recognition, vague criticism, scope or deadline pushback, or feedback recaps (use feedback-mastery); not for legal advice, formal complaints, PIPs, ratings, policy, or company-wide announcements.

findings.evidence: Read phrase-bank.md when the user needs lines to buy time in the room or to say they are triggered, and preparation-template.md when their goals, the time and place, or the way they are preparing needs work.
findings.fix: Split the readiness loads: read phrase-bank.md only for a line to buy time or to say they are triggered, and preparation-template.md only when goals, time and place, or a named preparation habit (over-preparing, winging it, preparing to attack or to avoid) needs work; for a short readiness question answer from this file and do not load either.

findings.evidence: Buying time lists seven near-equivalent lines ("Let me think about that", "Give me a moment", "Let me process it", "Can you say more", "Tell me more", "Bear with me", "Can we slow down").
findings.fix: Default to one line for a few seconds ("I want to respond thoughtfully. Give me a moment.") and one for a named break (SKILL.md Section 2), and keep the rest as alternatives only when the user asks for another wording.

findings.fix: Add an assertion that the plan includes a preparation step (facts versus motive, the other person's likely account, or a readiness check) so the expected output is fully verifiable.

findings.evidence: Readiness never delays urgent matters. Safety goes to Section 7 now. An urgent operational issue (a broken release, a customer at risk) is raised now with the decision owner, facts only
findings.fix: After the safety sentence, route harassment, discrimination, retaliation and formal proceedings to Section 7 immediately as well, and limit the raise-it-now exception to operational incidents that are not those cases.

findings.evidence: Four principles to return to: work from interests, not positions; acknowledge the emotions on both sides; look for options that work for both people; rebuild trust through small actions that are kept.
findings.fix: Move these four lines into the Gotchas as NEVER items with the failure they prevent (for example, never trade positions when the interests still overlap, because the meeting ends with no option either person can accept), or drop them and add a drop row to docs/audit/recovery/difficult-workplace-conversations/record.md.
